```{r migration-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(postrank)
source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE), local = TRUE)
one <- load_or_compute("tutorial_one")
two <- load_or_compute("tutorial_two")
```

The current version retains the posterior loss and strict input
definitions of the earlier 0.9 interface. The changes concern
one-criterion analyses, result extraction and presentation. This article
describes their implications for existing scripts, using stored results
without further optimization. The candidate has not been published.

## Result tables {#choose-the-table-you-need}

`as.data.frame(analysis)` now returns exactly `entity_id` and `grade` in
input entity order. This stable table supports joins and exports.
The row order is not a ranking: grade 1 has highest priority, and rows in the
same grade have their comparison withheld.

```{r migration-table}
as.data.frame(one)
```

Posterior means, interval endpoints and relation counts are available
through an explicit request for the report card:

```{r migration-card}
card <- as.data.frame(one, what = "report_card")
names(card)
```

The report card retains the row order and columns used for reporting. Its intervals are
marginal posterior intervals for the targets, not uncertainty intervals for
grade assignments. The interval level and source are recorded in `one$report_card`. An input carrying supplied intervals cannot reconstruct other
levels; CDE and KRW provide 90%, while Alabama provides 95%.

The two table forms can be exported separately:

```{r migration-export, eval=FALSE}
write.csv(as.data.frame(two), "grades.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame(two, what = "report_card"),
  "report-card.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## One-criterion and multiple-criterion weights {#start-with-one-criterion-then-declare-several-weights}

For a one-criterion `postrank()` analysis, the weight defaults to one
and may be omitted. This default applies to the one-call analysis. Lower-level functions such as
`postrank_problem()` and `postrank_evaluate()` still take the weights their
signatures require.

```{r migration-calls, eval=FALSE}
one <- postrank(pr_tutorial$one, tau = .2, G_max = 3L, backend = "highs")
two <- postrank(pr_tutorial$two,
  weights = c(score_A = .5, score_B = .5), tau = .2, G_max = 3L,
  backend = "highs")
```

Both tutorial inputs retain the same six sites and the same score-A law.
The two-criterion call changes the decision loss by adding score B. Loss
weights are declared preferences, not empirical reliability weights. Typed
settings provide a reusable policy specification. The policy is supplied
through either `settings` or the corresponding separate arguments;
conflicting specifications are rejected.

## Computational controls and status {#keep-computation-choices-explicit}

The default backend remains Gurobi. An explicit `backend` argument takes precedence over the
`postrank.backend` option. If the option is unset, Gurobi is used. HiGHS is an
explicit alternative, and an unavailable selection does not trigger a
fallback.

Progress messages are suppressed by default. A control with `verbose = NULL` reads
`postrank.verbose` when solving; explicit `TRUE` or `FALSE` overrides the
option. This affects progress messages, not numerical controls or results.
The separate `output` control governs solver output.

```{r migration-quiet, eval=FALSE}
quiet <- postrank_control(verbose = FALSE)
fit <- postrank(pr_tutorial$one, tau = .2, G_max = 3L,
  backend = "highs", control = quiet)
```

An ordinary fit is characterized by its validated grade, normalized
status and numerical bound. A backend's optimal label is qualified as feasible but uncertified
when a usable lower bound or sufficiently small gap is missing. Raw status
is retained. A time limit remains a time-limit status; a missing incumbent
remains missing and is not replaced with an all-withheld grade.

Withholding every pair is a feasible action in an ordinary at-most-G
problem. It has risk `tau` and no defined `E/N` because `N = 0`. An all-withheld grading is therefore distinguishable from a failed
optimization with no validated action.

## Display settings {#request-display-choices-without-changing-the-result}

Report-card plots now limit the default display to 30 rows, spreading the
selection across occupied grades. An explicit entity selection can show
more. Display labels are separate from stable entity IDs. Mean ordering
requires a single displayed criterion or an explicit `order_by` naming the
criterion that defines the order, on the plot or when preparing a card.

```{r migration-display, eval=FALSE}
postrank_plot_report_card(two, max_rows = 6L, ncol = 1L)
postrank_plot_report_card(two, entities = pr_tutorial$units$entity_id,
  entity_labels = c(A = "Site Alpha"), ncol = 1L)
postrank_plot_report_card(one, order = "mean")
postrank_plot_report_card(two, order = "mean", order_by = "score_A")
```

The plotting functions use prepared results. Pairwise-probability plots
show the stored directional-error matrix; they do not estimate new
probabilities. `postrank_plot_data()` returns the underlying tables for further
analysis without applying the plot's display selection. See the
[figure gallery](figure-gallery.html) and
[Figures and sensitivity analysis](a7-figures-sensitivity.html).

The exported `format_postrank_*_cli()` wrappers remain supported and match
`format()` with the same arguments. The call `format(x, width = 72, tier = 2)`
returns reusable text, whereas accessors provide values for calculations. `summary(x, details = TRUE)`
includes the detailed stored summary fields in its console display. The console display does not
define a schema for extracting values programmatically.

## Supplied comparison probabilities {#use-supplied-probabilities-without-inventing-draws}

`postrank_probabilities()` accepts already calculated tie-free pairwise
probabilities with an explicit event, zero-tie declaration, zero margin,
conditioning, target descriptions and source kind. It keeps raw values and
any permitted numerical correction. Optional means and intervals must refer
to those same oriented targets. These inputs do not provide a sample size,
ESS, MCSE or integration-error certificate.

Its initial decision scope is weighted at-most-G, including fixed-order
cuts. Native Gaussian and mixture problems have the same decision scope,
although their fixed-order cuts also accept an exact grade count. Draw
inputs support additional validated modes. The help for each operation specifies the available modes, which cannot
be inferred from the coefficient dimensions alone.

Genuine equality uses the separate `postrank_tie_*` domain and its
capability record. It does not reinterpret ordinary objects. Its strict
wrong-event and distinct-event withholding loss can have all-withhold risk
R0 below `tau`; raw disclosure and distinct-opportunity ratios have different
denominators. Tie-aware fits also qualify a raw optimal label when the
usable bound is missing or its gap is too wide. Their relative-gap scale
uses the action risk minus R0, preserving that separate loss offset. See [True ties and withheld comparisons](m4-ties-and-withholding.html).

## Historical inputs and result provenance {#keep-historical-inputs-and-results-identifiable}

The definitions of earlier strict constructors, schemas and scientific
payload identities are unchanged. Declaration checks do not retrospectively establish the validity of, or
modify, the scientific statements attached to an older object. Existing result views
represent absent historical information as unavailable. A new calculation
is required for quantities that were not stored.

Prepared documentation assets are tied to their generating package version
and source manifest. Reading an asset does not alter its provenance. Source changes require
regeneration of the affected assets through the builder.
This is separate from the archived research results inside case objects:
their producer versions remain historical facts.

The three case-study inputs retain their individual source conditions and
attribution. The CDE input preserves its source identification, KRW retains
the source's CC-BY-NC notice with no license version substituted, and Alabama
retains CC BY 4.0 attribution and change notices. The code license does not
override these third-party source conditions.

## Earlier articles {#find-the-earlier-articles}

The three earlier articles, `quickstart`, `inputs-and-producers` and
`baselines-and-the-cost-of-a-common-grade`, retain their distinct examples
and link to the Applied and Methods series where appropriate. [Getting started](a1-getting-started.html)
introduces the current interface; the Applied and Methods series provide
further practical and methodological detail.
